name: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar
role: Indian revolutionary, writer and Hindu nationalist ideologue; coined Hindutva; president of the Hindu Mahasabha (1937-1943)
summary: Savarkar (1883-1966) began as an armed revolutionary against British rule, was transported to the Andamans, and after his release in 1924 became the main ideologue of Hindu nationalism, defining a Hindu as one who holds India as both fatherland and holyland and treating the Hindus as a nation. As Hindu Mahasabha president he demanded one man one vote and equal citizenship with no communal electorates, an undivided India, Hindu militarisation, a machine-age nationalist economy that co-ordinated class interests, and war on caste untouchability, cow worship and superstition in the name of science, while describing Muslims as a hostile community and urging retaliation against enemy civilians in his history.
